questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code cleans up resources when a job fails? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A step in run_job exceeds its timeout and subprocess.run raises TimeoutExpired. In what order are the container and the workspace directory cleaned up?
choices: The workspace is deleted first, then the container is removed.
In parallel, since ExitStack runs all callbacks concurrently.
The container is removed first, then the workspace is deleted, because ExitStack unwinds in reverse order of entry.
Neither is cleaned up, because TimeoutExpired is not caught inside run_job.

questions.prompt: docker run itself fails with CalledProcessError inside started_container, after the workspace directory was created. What happens?
choices: The workspace directory is deleted and no docker rm is attempted, because the generator never reached its try block.
docker rm -f is attempted with a container id of None.
The workspace directory is left behind for debugging.
The error is logged and run_job returns "passed".

questions.prompt: A step fails and then docker rm -f also fails with CalledProcessError during cleanup. What reaches the caller of run_job?
choices: The CalledProcessError from docker rm, replacing the original error.
Both exceptions are combined into an ExceptionGroup.
Nothing, because failures during cleanup are always suppressed.
The original StepFailed, because the cleanup error is caught and logged and the exits after it still run.
